title: When agents need to agree
tagline: Two flows for the moments a team gets stuck: when nobody shares a picture of the task, and when there are real options and someone would just pick one.
needs: Two or more agents on one task, in a room with the conductor engine
The pairing or swarming course, or the same experience
takeaway: Knowing when a team needs to agree on the task and when it needs to agree on an answer, and the flow for each.
outcomes: Tell a team that doesn't share a picture of the task from one with real options
Run accord before work starts, and hand the summary to everyone
Run concord on a decision no one person should make alone

quiz.question: Two agents keep building different things for a task called "rename". Which flow?
options: Concord: they need to pick one approach
Accord: they don't mean the same thing by the task
Neither: let them finish and compare
quiz.why: The work collided because one word meant two things. That's a picture of the task to agree on, before there are options to pick between.

modules.title: Get on the same page: accord

video.about: Three agents say what a task is. Accord merges their points, finds a word they use in two senses, and saves one summary.

quiz.question: Accord flags a point only one member made. What happens to it?
options: It's dropped, since the others didn't agree
The conductor asks the others to vote on it
It stays in the summary as an open item for someone to settle
quiz.why: Accord records and flags; it never decides. An open item is exactly what a person or a later step should look at.

video.about: Three agents each suggest an option and rate them all. The least happy one proposes a fix, and everyone settles on it.

quiz.question: Options A, B and C are rated. A's lowest rating is 55, B's is 40, C's is 62. The bar is 70. What happens?
options: A is picked, since it has the highest average
C is the pick so far, and the member who rated it 62 is asked for a fix
The run stops: nothing cleared the bar
quiz.why: Concord picks the option whose least happy member is happiest, then asks that member to fix it. It stops only after two fixes, or when someone isn't answering.
